reviews.title: Focused on the wrong thing
reviews.text:
This app is extremely lacking in the UX department. It’s very difficult to perform basic tasks that are extremely simple in other apps. Writing a review for a read book that’s already in your finished list was so difficult, you have to click on the star rating inside your finished list. You should be able to just go to a book and see your review for it from the search results.

Also that fact they allow Goodreads import, but have no export feature feels parasitic. If you allow people to switch to you, you should make it easy for them to try and switch back if they’re unsatisfied.

I understand the app is about the social aspect of reading, but there needs to be a major focus on improving how simple tasks are completed.

reviews.title: Love idea, but they don’t allow exports
reviews.text: I liked fable for a while, but since they’ve started leaning into AI features so heavily, I was feeling less and less good about using the app. But guess what? Fable doesn’t even allow you to export your data like other apps, so either you have to transfer manually or lose your reading data. I don’t appreciate when apps lock you out of your own data, so I guess this is a reminder for me that I should check the way apps own my data. I would’ve kept the app and still used some features if they allowed export but guess not. Really disappointed at this scammy practices

reviews.title: Great to have another app for readers but…
reviews.text: It’s lovely to have a new app for readers, the app offers in depth analytics of what you’ve read through the year and you can get some insights into your own reading tastes. However, there are a couple of things that prevent me from fully switching over and using Fable more. My issues are related to the UX/UI. The app is very dark, there is no light mode and the black background with white text is very hard on the eyes. I have to strain to use it which makes me want to click off the app as quickly as possible. The second bit is around how difficult it is to update reading status of my current reading list. Too much focus on the “I read today streak” which I personally don’t care for as it’s one of those things that makes reading into a competitive sport and takes away from the enjoyment. I would prefer if there was option to disable it and instead to have a quick and easy flow to changing the status of the books I am reading. This app has a lot of potential but it’s not pleasant to use. It’s too busy, too much going on. Too distracting from what it’s supposed to promote: reading.

reviews.title: Disappointingly hateful
reviews.text:
I wanted to like this app. Even tried a month of premium to see the extra features, I was so excited! Goodreads can be a bit dull after so many years so I was looking for an alternative. 

I was immediately impressed. A whole app for book lovers?! With added features for TV and movies. Dream come true! 

But like with every app with a social media aspect, the hate I started to see in the posts.. I was seeing posts with lists of authors that should be “banned” and “if you read this author block me now”

There is a lot of left leaning users, which is fine. I believe we all can believe in what we want to. We can get along. But not if it’s continuously all the time from so many users. I didn’t think after a month I would have so many people blocked that I didn’t even talk to. It’s just the attitude and vibe of the app. I don’t want to see politics and hate for those who think differently than them. I don’t care about it, I care about the stories and the books. 

I witnessed folks I did converse with get reported and kicked off for quoting out of books deemed by the mass of fable as not appropriate to the left.. 

That’s where I had to draw the line. There truly is no free speech in this app.

I’m keeping with Goodreads. Where there is no social aspect, full of a bunch of air heads. Just you and your books.

reviews.title: Good app, bad business decisions
reviews.text:
I’ve been on Goodreads for a long time before moving to StoryGraph. But that app struggled to convince me and in my search for something different I found Fable. It’s been amazing, for the first time in my life I’m reading every single day and I’m about to reach the 1yr streak. The book clubs are incredible, I’m genuinely making friends through books and wild stories… 

But I don’t know who is in charge of this thing because they’re making some really questionable business decisions. The last of these is removing private messages out of the blue without giving notice to its users. I’ve never received a notification, their change logs don’t show anywhere that this happened at the end of February, according to their support team. I have lost entire conversations with people where we were sharing book suggestions or other stuff people talk about! Now everything needs to happen out in public because it was easier than implementing moderation. 

Absolutely appalling behavior.
I will definitely stop recommending the app like I had for the past year and a half. I would stop ising it altogether if it wasn’t for the community of readers I have found, but likely, we can all (re)group on other platforms with very little convincing.
